title: Kierston & KierstonBench: Simulation of Allentown, PA and Evaluation of Language Models in Crime Investigation and Surveillance Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2611.04785v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models are candidates for collecting and analyzing records in criminal investigations and mass surveillance. Their capability and accuracy in this work cannot currently be measured. Real deployments lack the ground truth needed to score a model's conclusions, and no benchmark evaluates these capabilities in a simulated environment. We present Kierston, a city-scale simulation engine, and KierstonBench, a benchmark that tests these capabilities against known simulated events. Kierston models approximately 125,000 residents of Allentown, Pennsylvania, generating their daily activities and the telecommunications, financial, administrative and license-plate records that surveillance and investigative systems collect about them. translated_title: Kierston 与 KierstonBench：宾夕法尼亚州阿伦敦市的模拟及语言模型在犯罪调查与监控任务中的评估
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型是刑事调查与大规模监控中收集和分析记录的候选工具，但其在这些工作中的能力与准确性目前无法衡量：实际部署缺乏评估模型结论所需的真实标准，也没有任何基准能在模拟环境中评估这些能力。我们提出了城市级模拟引擎 Kierston，以及针对已知模拟事件测试上述能力的基准 KierstonBench。Kierston 模拟了宾夕法尼亚州阿伦敦市约 125,000 名居民，生成他们的日常活动，以及监控与调查系统所收集的电信、金融、行政和车牌记录。这些记录源自共同的行为时间线，并分布在代表不同服务提供商的各个数据源中。模型通过受限的记录访问接口开展调查，对观测记录进行关联……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了城市级模拟引擎 Kierston 与配套基准 KierstonBench，通过模拟宾州阿伦敦市约12.5万名居民的日常活动及多源记录，首次实现了对大语言模型在犯罪调查与监控任务中能力的可量化评估。
en_tdlr: The paper presents Kierston, a city-scale simulation engine modeling ~125,000 residents of Allentown, PA along with their multi-source records, together with KierstonBench, the first benchmark enabling measurable evaluation of language models on crime investigation and surveillance tasks.
